LEARNING PATH LESSON · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

Yellow — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson puts yellow where it teaches best: on the table. Banana, sweetcorn, egg yolk — snack time is the fastest color classroom in the house.

What is this?

Yellow is a color — the color of sunshine and bananas — and this card carries it alone, bright from edge to edge.

What does it mean?

Two beats make the word bounce — yeh-low — and lellow is a normal, useful first draft. Keep the bounce; the consonants will land on their own.

What does the child need to know?

Food teaches colors faster than anything printed: hold up the banana, say the word, take the bite. Three repetitions at snack time outperform ten at the table with cards.

Why this matters

Yellow hides in plain sight all day — ducks, sun, cheese, trucks. A color with a food anchor gets a guaranteed daily rehearsal slot.

What it teaches

Color naming through taste and smell (multisensory beats visual alone), two-syllable word practice, and noticing-brightness language.

Words to learn

yellowsunbananabrightducksnack

Say this to your child

“"Yellow! Bright yellow, like the sun. Look — a banana! Is it yellow? Yes! Can you say yellow? Yeh-low. What else can we find that is yellow?"”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and say yellow — then hold up a real banana beside it: same color, one word.
  2. Run a snack-time yellow hunt: banana, sweetcorn, a square of cheese. Name the color as each one lands on the plate.
  3. Hunt yellow around the house afterwards — the duck in the bath, a yellow toy, a flower on the walk.
  4. When lellow arrives, echo yellow clearly once and hand over the banana; the correction is your pronunciation, never their feelings.
  5. Keep one yellow food in the snack rotation all week so the word has a standing appointment every day.

Look closer at the picture

Yellow owns this card from edge to edge, with the word yellow printed underneath. Ask your child to say the word while laying a hand flat on the color.

Ask your child

"What color is this card?" "What color is your banana?" "Can you find something yellow in the bath?" "Is the sun yellow?"

What your child can say or do

"Lellow!" with a banana held aloft, or a pointing finger at every duck within range. Expect the bath to become a yellow classroom for a week — rubber ducks are enthusiastic assistants.

Out in the real world

Bananas, corn on the cob, dandelions, school buses and the sun itself — yellow keeps appointments all day. The food version has the advantage of being eatable.

Try it together

Sunshine picnic: lay a yellow cloth or tea towel on the floor and fill it only with yellow snacks and toys. Everything on the blanket must earn its place by being yellow.

Understanding check

Ask what color the card is, then what color the banana is. Two yellows — or two lellows — passes completely. A spontaneous yellow! at the fruit bowl ends the assessment early.

Parent tips

Snack-time teaching beats table teaching every time at two — appetite opens ears. Keep saying the full word even when lellow is adorable; the two-beat bounce is what they are practising.

Staying safe

Food-based color play needs the usual kitchen care: sit down for eating, cut rounds small, and keep the hunt away from the hot stove and the kettle.

This lesson pairs with the Yellow flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shapes (Toddler 3).
